name: forge
description: Agent-engineering workflow skills for Claude Code, Codex, and opencode — twenty-five fg-* skills: the three-stage loop (fg-ask → fg-run → fg-done, the retro decided inside the seal) plus outside-the-loop utilities including fg-learn (batch promotion), including fg-security (vendored security audit) and fg-debug (vendored diagnosis only: active failures return to fg-run; independent diagnoses route by size, durable eval, and all-exit safe cleanup). Includes fg-monitor, a Node 22+ read-only dashboard scoped to the current Claude Code project, branch and session; localhost by default, explicit external binding, first-launch retention choice and owner-session shutdown. fg-rules reviews evidence-backed project rules before writing, stores adopted changes in top-level .forge/rules/, preserves manual edits, and connects rules to ordinary coding through existing project instructions; fg-map describes current code, while rules guide future work. Connection verification is distinct from observed loading and does not guarantee compliance. fg-verify builds or refreshes a project-local verification skill (verify-<app>, under .claude/skills/) that drives the app the way a user does and captures evidence, plus a feature map of the journeys it can prove — it builds the tool fg-run's UAT uses rather than verifying anything itself; evidence stays in a self-ignored .forge/verify/, the UAT reads the skill's files so no restart is needed, a drive that needs a human halts as an unverifiable UAT instead of failing, and unattended drives never build one (adapted in concept from pstack, MIT).

interface.shortDescription: Plan, execute, learn, and seal agent work
interface.longDescription: A shared Claude Code and Codex workflow for turning one task into a reviewed plan, verified execution, retained learning, and a sealed result.
defaultPrompt: Start a new task with Forge.
